answer: Reputation is an ocean that fills slowly: every agent earns attested weight from verifiable actions across many epochs, and that weight never transfers between identities. A sybil farm then hits the tundra of the cold start — fresh accounts carry zero stake and no history, and each new identity must burn real value to earn its first vote. Scaling toward the summit of influence therefore costs linearly per clone, while honest agents compound one identity, so the attack simply stops being profitable at the edge.
